title: A Skin Cell That Feels Force

scenes.tts: A cell in your skin is not a neuron. Yet it helps a nerve keep firing while you press. This is the Merkel cell. In mouse skin it sits in the basal epidermis, beside the ending of one slowly adapting type one afferent. Lineage tracing in mouse embryos shows it arises from epidermal progenitors, not from neurons.

scenes.tts: In cultured Merkel cells from young mice, pressing evokes a current. The current averaged three hundred seventy picoamps at its peak. At steady state it averaged twenty picoamps, about five point four percent of the peak. When Piezo two was deleted from skin epithelium, none of thirteen cultured Merkel cells had a detectable current.

scenes.visual: A large Merkel cell with a Piezo2 chip in its membrane is pressed; a decaying current trace is drawn from 370 pA to 20 pA with tau 8 ms; then the chip is crossed out and thirteen empty circles show no current.

scenes.tts: So the cell's own current is mostly brief. Yet the afferent it drives fires for as long as the touch lasts. The dynamic phase is the fast firing at the onset. The static phase is the sustained firing that follows, with irregular intervals. How a brief current becomes sustained firing is not explained by these data.

scenes.tts: In an ex vivo mouse skin and nerve preparation, light that depolarizes only Merkel cells was enough to make the afferent fire. Light that hyperpolarizes them suppressed the sustained firing to a touch. In the reported experiment, from three units, median firing fell tenfold.

scenes.visual: Cell and afferent at left; green light on the cell with no touch makes spikes appear in a lane; red light during a held touch thins a steady spike lane to a tenth, labelled in this sketch.

scenes.tts: In the mouse two receptor model, the Merkel cell shapes the sustained firing, and the ending keeps its own mechanosensitive machinery. When Piezo two was deleted from epithelium, dynamic responses stayed similar to controls and normal sustained firing was lost. In mice without Merkel cells, afferents still respond to touch, but sustained firing is cut short. Peak firing fell from two hundred thirty eight to seventy nine hertz, down sixty six point eight percent in group means. A developmental deletion of the cells cannot say through which mechanism.
scenes.caption: In the mouse two-receptor model, the Merkel cell shapes the sustained firing, and the ending keeps its own mechanosensitive machinery. When Piezo2 was deleted from epithelium, dynamic responses stayed similar to controls and normal sustained firing was lost. In mice without Merkel cells, afferents still respond to touch, but sustained firing is cut short. Peak firing fell from 238 to 79 Hz, down 66.8% in group means. A developmental deletion of the cells cannot say through which mechanism.

scenes.tts: What crosses the gap from cell to nerve? Three accounts exist, each in its own preparation. Noradrenaline, in mouse touch domes. Serotonin, in mouse whisker Merkel cells. Protons acting on ASIC channels, in rodent whisker follicles. The adrenergic account is neither settled nor refuted. Keep this: in mouse skin, a skin cell senses force, and its transmitter is still open.
